candidates.name: airbnb/knowledge-repo
candidates.what_it_holds: Airbnb's own official open-source platform (the one referenced by Airbnb's Data Science blog era) for publishing 'knowledge posts' — Jupyter/IPython notebooks, R Markdown, Markdown, or linked Google Docs — with a review workflow and a feed/stats dashboard. Repo directories: knowledge_repo/ (core app), knowledge_repo_v2/, docs/, docker/, scripts/, tests/. It is infrastructure, not a dataset: no committed Airbnb business data or analysis outputs ship in the repo itself, only the tool Airbnb used internally to run its knowledge-sharing feed.
candidates.why_useful: Directly answers the 'Airbnb Data Science blog notebooks' theme hint — this is the actual platform, confirmed still on github.com/airbnb. No forecasting value on its own since it carries no data, but worth recording as the authoritative source-of-truth repo in case any public knowledge_repo instance (Airbnb's own or a fork) still serves archived posts/notebooks with real KPI analysis.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 (per repo norms; not independently re-verified this pass)
candidates.last_activity: actively maintained as of the org repo listing (not independently dated this pass)

candidates.name: tomslee/airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: Tom Slee's original Airbnb listings scraper — the direct historical predecessor to Inside Airbnb. Python scripts + PostgreSQL/PostGIS schema to survey listings by neighborhood, zip code, or bounding box. MIT licensed. Maintainer states 'I am no longer maintaining this script'; last substantive activity ~2019, broke against Airbnb's page-layout changes. No committed CSV/data dump found in the repo itself (data historically lived in the author's own PostgreSQL instances / a separate personal site, not in this repo).
candidates.why_useful: This is the tool that produced some of the only pre-2015/pre-Inside-Airbnb-era STR listings snapshots that exist anywhere; if any fork or mirror of the author's actual output data surfaced elsewhere it would fill gap #1 (historical/archived dumps pre-2023). As shipped here it is code only, and it scrapes airbnb.com directly, which is a ToS decision for a human per repo rules — catalogued as method, not run.
candidates.time_coverage: ~2014-2017 (era the tool was actively run, per author's own historical write-ups; not in-repo)
candidates.size_hint: scraper codebase only, no committed data

candidates.name: deaneeth/airbnb-market-intelligence-pipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: Reproducible, config-driven pipeline that pulls Inside Airbnb's public detailed-listings/calendar/reviews/neighbourhood files (currently configured for Amsterdam, snapshot 2026-06-15) and turns them into typed Parquet, a DuckDB star schema, SQL summaries, ML benchmarks, and a Streamlit dashboard. Explicitly excludes raw/staged/processed data files from version control (pull-only, no committed data). Adding a new city is a one-line configs/cities.yml change, no code change. 69 commits, active as of July 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Duplicates what we already hold (Inside Airbnb panel) in substance, but the config-driven multi-city harness pattern is a clean reference for turning a raw Inside Airbnb pull into an analysis-ready store fast, if we ever want to add a market beyond our current 13/34/120-market panels.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Inside Airbnb panel we already hold (13-city + 34-market + 120-market cohorts)
candidates.geography: Amsterdam (configurable to any Inside Airbnb city)

candidates.name: everythingscraper/airbnb-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: An Apify Actor described as 'STR analytics on tap — occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, and 12-month calendars from Airbnb', i.e. a hosted scraper that returns realized-style occupancy/ADR/RevPAR metrics and forward 12-month calendars per listing/market on demand. No data committed to the repo — it is a paid-actor front end scraping airbnb.com directly.
candidates.why_useful: If ever run (a human ToS call, not for this pass), this is one of the only tools that claims to expose something close to realized ADR/occupancy per market — directly on gap #2. Catalogued as method only per repo rules; not run.
candidates.size_hint: Apify actor wrapper, no committed dataset

candidates.name: dtrungtin/actor-airbnb-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Another Apify-style actor extracting publicly-available Airbnb listing data (prices, calendars, host info) directly from airbnb.com at scale.
candidates.why_useful: Same class as everythingscraper above — a method for pulling calendar/price data per listing/market that could speak to realized ADR/occupancy (gap #2) or booking lead-time/cancellation patterns (gap #3) if the calendar payload includes booked-vs-available state history. Not run; ToS decision for a human.

candidates.name: luminati-io/Airbnb-dataset-samples (Bright Data)
candidates.what_it_holds: Bright Data's sample dataset repo: ~1,000+ Airbnb listings pulled via their commercial scraping API, provided as a free sample with a pointer to the full paid dataset/API on Bright Data's own platform.
candidates.why_useful: Only a small free sample is committed; the substantive data sits behind Bright Data's paid product. Marginal value as a one-time cross-check of listing counts/prices in a handful of markets, not a real time series.
candidates.license: sample data, commercial product license for full dataset
candidates.time_coverage: single pull, undated in fetched content
candidates.size_hint: 1,000+ listing rows in the free sample

candidates.name: jsvine/waybackpack
candidates.what_it_holds: CLI tool to download the entire set of Wayback-Machine-archived snapshots for a given URL (all timestamps, all captured assets) via the Internet Archive API.
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose Wayback tooling named explicitly in gap #17 ('Wayback Machine tooling (archived airbnb.com pages, archived AirDNA market pages)'). Could pull archived newsroom.airbnb.com press-release pages or archived AirDNA/STR market pages for point-in-time text/price snapshots, subject to the Wayback Machine's own airbnb.com exclusions noted by other search results.
candidates.license: MIT (typical for this project; not independently re-verified)

candidates.name: edgi-govdata-archiving/wayback
candidates.what_it_holds: Python API client for the Internet Archive Wayback Machine (part of the Environmental Data & Governance Initiative's toolset), for fetching historical snapshots of any URL programmatically.
candidates.why_useful: Same class as waybackpack above, more actively maintained (EDGI is a live project) — usable for pulling dated snapshots of newsroom.airbnb.com, ir.airbnb.com guidance pages, or third-party STR-data-vendor market pages (AirDNA, Key Data, etc.) for point-in-time reconstruction, directly serving gap #17.
candidates.last_activity: actively maintained per EDGI norms; not independently dated this pass

notes: This theme was heavily hampered by tooling failures rather than a genuine absence of results: the session's shared WebSearch budget (200/200) was already exhausted by other scouts before this agent's first call, so every WebSearch query failed immediately and all findings here came from WebFetch against search-engine result pages instead. Google and GitHub's own /search endpoint both returned HTTP 429 (GitHub's search 429 carried a 1-hour Retry-After, so gh-style repo search was unusable all pass); DuckDuckGo (both html. and lite.) served CAPTCHA challenges every time; Mojeek and Ecosia returned 403; Marginalia self-throttled as 'aggressive bot activity'. Only Bing (partially — it ignored site: filters and mostly returned airbnb.com property pages) and Brave (worked well, no site: filter needed) returned usable result lists. Recommend future scouts on this modality lead with Brave (search.brave.com/search?q=...&source=web) rather than Google/DDG/Mojeek/Ecosia given today's blocking pattern. Substantively: the airbnb GitHub org (verified via /orgs/airbnb/repositories) contains zero data-bearing repos relevant to ABNB forecasting — it's all engineering/UI tooling (lottie, visx, mavericks, streamalert, airpal, aerosolve, knowledge-repo, style guides). There is no 'insideairbnb' GitHub org (confirmed 404) — Inside Airbnb's actual data lives on their own CDN, not GitHub, consistent with what CONTEXT.md already describes as our access path. 'Airbnb Newsroom scraper' as a literal search term produced zero on-topic hits across every engine tried (GitHub topics for airbnb-newsroom and press-release-scraper are both literally empty) — nobody appears to have built or topic-tagged a public newsroom.airbnb.com scraper on GitHub. The 'Airbnb Data Science blog notebooks' angle resolves to airbnb/knowledge-repo as the one real corporate artifact; the community-notebook results under that query are all the excluded genre (single-city Kaggle/Udacity/IBM-capstone re-analyses of one already-known dataset) and were not catalogued. Two direct-scrape Apify actors (everythingscraper, dtrungtin) surfaced that explicitly claim occupancy/ADR/RevPAR extraction from airbnb.com — flagged as medium potential on gap #2 but deliberately not run per repo rules (touching airbnb.com beyond sanctioned sources is a ToS call for a human). Ran out of remaining WebFetch budget before covering the job-postings/headcount and awesome-list angles for this theme (both queries hit Brave 429 near the end of the run) — a follow-up scout should retry 'github airbnb job postings headcount glassdoor' and 'awesome-airbnb open source list' once rate limits reset.
